tips.greetings: 💡 Vietnamese has tones — the same syllable in different tones means different things. Don't worry, locals will appreciate any attempt.
tips.food: 💡 Phở is pronounced more like "fuh" than "foe". Street food is safe — follow the queue of locals.
tips.directions: 💡 Always use Grab in Vietnam — fixed price, no negotiation needed. Cross roads slowly and steadily, traffic flows around you.
tips.numbers: 💡 Prices are in thousands (ngàn) — "ba mươi" (30) usually means 30,000 đồng (~$1.20).
tips.shopping: Bargain in markets. Count the zeros on a dong price before you agree.
tips.medical: Call 115 for an ambulance. Buy bottled water.
tips.immigration: Keep the entry stamp and have a hotel address written down.
tips.hotel: Ask whether breakfast is included, and whether the room faces a noisy street.
tips.transport: Grab works in the big cities. Prefer it to a street taxi.

pronGuide.title: Vietnamese Sounds
tips: 6 tones marked by accent marks — flat (no mark) is your safe default
Rising tone (á) goes up, like asking a question in English
The letter D is "z" in northern Vietnam, "y" in the south
Ơ sounds like "uh" in bird, Ư is like "oo" with rounded lips forward

culture.rule: Use two hands when giving or receiving
culture.note: Especially with elders. Giving money, business cards, or gifts with one hand is considered casual or disrespectful.

culture.rule: Remove shoes at homes and some temples
culture.note: Look for shoes at the entrance — it's the universal signal. Always follow the lead of your host.
Avoid public confrontation or expressing frustration. Criticism should be gentle and private — public embarrassment is taken seriously.
Vietnamese society is family-first and deeply Confucian. Address older people respectfully and defer to them in social situations.
Smile, be friendly, and start at 50–60% of asking price. It's a social ritual — enjoy it.

culture.rule: Dress modestly at temples and pagodas
culture.note: Cover shoulders and knees. Most temples have wraps available to borrow.

money.rule: USD is also accepted in tourist areas
money.note: Especially in Hanoi's Old Quarter and Ho Chi Minh City. However, you'll often get worse value than paying in dong.

money.rule: Vietcombank ATMs are best for foreigners
money.note: Look for Vietcombank or Techcombank. Withdrawal limits vary — try ₫3,000,000 (~$120) per transaction.
Ben Thanh Market and Hanoi's Old Quarter — start at 40–50% of asking. Walking away often brings the price down further.

money.rule: Exchange at banks or official kiosks only
money.note: Street money changers sometimes shortchange tourists by using trick counting. Always use a licensed exchanger.

money.rule: Tipping is not traditional but appreciated
money.note: ₫20,000–50,000 at restaurants is generous. Guides and drivers who perform well deserve more.

food.name: Phở
food.what: Rice noodle soup with beef or chicken, herbs, lime, and bean sprouts — the national breakfast dish
food.tip: Add basil, bean sprouts, and a squeeze of lime. Ask for 'tái' (rare beef) to cook in the hot broth.

food.name: Bánh mì
food.what: Vietnamese baguette stuffed with pork, pâté, pickled vegetables, coriander, and chilli — a French colonial legacy done better
food.tip: The best ones are from street carts, not cafés. Bánh Mì 25 in Hanoi is famous.

food.name: Gỏi cuốn
food.what: Fresh (unfried) spring rolls with shrimp, pork, herbs, and rice noodles wrapped in rice paper
food.tip: Dip in peanut sauce, not fish sauce. A lighter option when the heat gets to you.

food.name: Bánh xèo
food.what: Sizzling rice flour crêpe filled with pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts — eaten wrapped in lettuce with dipping sauce
food.tip: Tear pieces off with your hands and wrap in the accompanying lettuce and herbs.

food.name: Cà phê trứng
food.what: Hanoi's famous egg coffee — a thick, custardy foam of whisked egg yolk and condensed milk over espresso
food.tip: Try it at Café Giang or Café Dinh in Hanoi's Old Quarter — the originators.

food.name: Sinh tố (fruit smoothie)
food.what: Fresh tropical fruit blended with condensed milk and ice — avocado, mango, soursop, dragonfruit
food.tip: Available everywhere for under ₫30,000. The avocado smoothie (sinh tố bơ) is surprisingly delicious.

safety.note: Roads are chaotic with motorbikes flowing in all directions. Cross slowly and steadily — traffic flows around you. Never freeze or run.
Metered taxis frequently overcharge tourists. Grab shows the fixed price upfront — use it every time.
Keep bags on your inside shoulder away from the road. Phone thieves on motorbikes target people looking at their phones while walking.
Sleight-of-hand counting tricks are common. Use bank ATMs or official exchange kiosks only.

safety.rule: Check sea conditions in coastal areas
safety.note: Red flag days at Đà Nẵng and Mũi Né beaches mean dangerous conditions — local lifeguards enforce this.

apps.name: Grab
apps.desc: Essential in Vietnam — fixed-price rides, food delivery, and bike-hailing all in one.

apps.name: Google Maps
apps.desc: Works well in Vietnam. Download Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi offline maps.

apps.name: Google Translate
apps.desc: Camera mode reads Vietnamese menus. Download the offline language pack.

apps.name: Wise
apps.desc: Best exchange rates for spending dong. Set up your account before travelling.

apps.name: Klook
apps.desc: Ha Long Bay cruises, cooking classes, and motorbike tours — book in advance.

apps.name: Booking.com
apps.desc: Free cancellation filters. Vietnam has excellent budget guesthouses (nhà nghỉ).
